robot-dog.title: Robot Dog
captions: Quadrupedal robot, designed and coded from scratch. The culmination of multiple leg-linkage prototypes, a full CAD assembly, and custom control code.
Inverse kinematics maps the three degrees of freedom per leg to a full 6 DOF control of the body.
Walks, and rotates, wiggles and gyrates smoothly, blending motion across all of its axes of freedom.

pid-seesaw.title: PID Seesaw
captions: Ball-balancing PID seesaw. An infrared sensor tracks the ball, and a servo tilts the beam to keep it balanced at the center.
Resistant to disturbances. Knock the ball away and the PID controller pulls it right back to center.
The product of many iterations, starting years ago with a LEGO prototype.

micromanipulator.title: Micromanipulator
micromanipulator.tag: Closed-loop stepper control, 100 nm theoretical resolution
micromanipulator.summary: A low-cost, 3D-printed alternative to industrial micromanipulators, which cost $1,000 to $60,000. Geometric microstepping and a magnetic-gearing encoder bring angular error down to about 0.0005°, which allows a theoretical end-effector resolution of 100 nm. Physical testing of that resolution is the next step.
captions: A DIY, $200 version of a $10,000–60,000 industrial device that moves on the nanometer scale with comparable accuracy.
A new microstepping formula I derived eliminates up to 1/25 of a full step of error, 0.072°, more than 140 times the 0.0005° accuracy the system achieves.
A row of 17 axially magnetized magnets multiplies encoder resolution 8.5 times.
Closed-loop PID control holds angular error to 0.0005°, for a theoretical 100 nm resolution at the tip.

slides.caption: Geometric microstepping
points: Standard microstepping assumes a motor's two phases sit **90°** apart. In this motor they sit **45°** apart.
So I derived a new formula that sets the coil currents quadrant by quadrant.
It erases up to **1/25** of a full step of error. That's **0.072°** on a 1.8° motor, over **140×** the system's accuracy.

slides.caption: Magnetic gearing for the encoder
points: A magnetic encoder reads the angle of a field. A normal magnet turns that field just once per revolution.
Here an arc of **17** alternating magnets rides on the motor horn, past the encoder. Each N‑S pair spins the field a full circle.
That's **8.5** field turns per revolution. The **21‑bit** MT6835 now spends all its counts on 1/8.5 of a turn, for **8.5×** the resolution.
Closed loop cuts error from **0.08°** to **0.0045°**. PID takes it to **0.0005°**, a theoretical **100 nm** at the tip.

ship-in-a-bottle.title: Ship in a Bottle
captions: A ship built from scratch and assembled inside the bottle.
Extreme precision, with custom tools bent from clothes hangers to reach through the neck.
Made from a block of basswood, wooden dowels, 22-gauge wire, sewing thread, paint and paper.

chess-engine.title: Chess Engine
captions: My first and longest-running project, started four years ago and improved ever since.
A pure-Python engine built on bitboards and minimax search, with iterative deepening, alpha-beta pruning and a transposition table.
NNUE evaluation, a small neural network that updates incrementally as pieces move, replaces handcrafted heuristics.
Rated 2000+ Elo against other bots on Lichess.

media.caption: The engine playing a game as Black.

hybrid-networks.title: EvoGrad
hybrid-networks.tag: Hybrid neural networks: NEAT with gradient descent
hybrid-networks.summary: A neural-network library where evolution designs the network and gradient descent trains it. KAN-style learnable activation functions train alongside the weights.

media.caption: CartPole, solved by EvoGrad. The best network of each generation, all from the same start. By generation 4 it balances the pole for all 500 steps, from every one of 100 test starts.
One curve, fitted three ways.
points: **Evolution only.** Still a crude step after 300 generations.
**+ Gradient descent.** Hits the target in 15 generations.
**+ Learnable activations.** 500× lower error than evolution alone, in one generation.

media.caption: Networks evolved for XOR, sin(x) and a damped sine. Blue edges are positive weights, red negative.

tennis-simulation.title: Tennis Statistics Library
tennis-simulation.tag: Bayesian updates, Monte Carlo, live-traded on prediction markets
tennis-simulation.summary: Simulates tennis matches and updates win probability live with Bayesian statistics. Its point-importance module was tested in live trading on prediction markets at the 2026 US Open, sizing positions up before the points most likely to swing the match.

media.caption: One simulated match, point by point. Win probability updates live, and each point's importance shows below.
Point importance
points: **One match.** The biggest points, marked by who won them.
**Serve.** Players win less often on serve as the stakes rise.

protein-classifier.title: Alzheimer's Protein Classifier
protein-classifier.summary: A support vector machine over genomic and proteomic data that classifies whether a protein sequence is associated with Alzheimer's disease, with controls to correct for sequence length bias. Accuracy: 80.3%.

media.caption: Accuracy and sequence length bias
points: **Fig. 2.1** Protein model: as the data shrinks to 10%, raw accuracy falls from **~89%** to **~78%**, adjusted from **~80%** to **~69%**.
**Fig. 2.2** Genome model: raw accuracy stays near **95–97%**, but adjusted accuracy is only **~50–53%**.
**Fig. 3.1** Alzheimer's-associated proteins skew shorter, peaking near **200–300** amino acids against **400–500** for the rest.
**Fig. 3.2** Non-Alzheimer's genes are dominated by a spike of **~17,000** sequences under **100** nucleotides.
Length differs between the classes, so the classifier controls for it: **80.3%** accuracy.

world-models.title: Plan Shallow While You Learn
world-models.summary: Co-authored paper accepted to the Continual World Models workshop at NeurIPS 2026 in Sydney. It shows that while a world model adapts to changed physics, planning compute should favor breadth over depth to maximize returns.

media.caption: Yann LeCun and Fei-Fei Li have papers in the same 42-paper workshop. [See for yourself!](https://neurips.cc/virtual/2026/loc/sydney/workshop/137499)

Drag compresses the optimal imagination depth from H=12 to H=6 (Fig. 1). Moving the same budget from depth to refinement iterations gains +2.4 to +11.2 return across the drag tiers (Fig. 2) and leads the deep default in all six deployment panels (Fig. 3).

world-models.fullTitle: Plan Shallow While You Learn: Reallocating Planning Compute During World-Model Adaptation

asteroid-orbit.title: Orbit Determination and Photometry of the Mars-crossing Asteroid 6249 Jennifer (1991 JF1)
captions: In a team of three, determined the orbit of asteroid 6249 Jennifer from original observations over three nights.
Plate solving gave its celestial coordinates, and the Method of Gauss turned them into orbital elements.
Written up as a technical paper, with the observations submitted to the Minor Planet Center.
The paper can’t be shared publicly under the Summer Science Program’s policies.
Calibrated 60-second exposure from a Las Cumbres Observatory telescope, with the computed orbit and photometric fits.

media.caption: Calibrated 60-second exposure from a Las Cumbres Observatory telescope, with the computed orbit and photometric fits.

asteroid-orbit.fullTitle: Orbit Determination and Photometry of the Mars-crossing Asteroid 6249 Jennifer (1991 JF1)
